# Impact analysis: current tariff (GLM-A) to proposed tariff (GLM-B)

*Generated by `src/impact/dislocation.py` from `reports/tables/impact_*.csv`.*

## Who moves

Both tariffs raise the same total premium (ratio 1.000000), so this is a redistribution. 32.3% of exposure moves by less than 5%; 12.4% moves by more than 20%.

| Change | Policies | Exposure | Mean change | Holdout observed / current | Holdout observed / proposed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| < -20% | 31,736 | 4.0% | -28.8% | 0.69 | 1.00 |
| -20% to -10% | 100,647 | 17.3% | -13.5% | 0.85 | 0.98 |
| -10% to -5% | 71,468 | 11.1% | -6.7% | 0.87 | 0.93 |
| -5% to +5% | 202,221 | 32.3% | -2.0% | 0.94 | 0.96 |
| +5% to +10% | 111,319 | 15.8% | +7.6% | 1.28 | 1.19 |
| +10% to +20% | 88,589 | 11.2% | +13.4% | 1.24 | 1.09 |
| > +20% | 72,011 | 8.4% | +26.6% | 1.16 | 0.89 |

Largest moves by factor level (at least 2,000 policy-years):

| Level | Mean change | Holdout claims | Observed / current | Observed / proposed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BonusMalus_band 66-70 | +18.2% | 203 | 1.08 | 0.91 |
| BonusMalus_band 61-65 | -10.9% | 395 | 0.88 | 0.98 |
| VehBrand_grp B12 | +7.2% | 847 | 0.99 | 0.99 |

Most affected segment: BonusMalus_band=100-110 & VehBrand_grp=B12 (-31.7%, 1,705 policy-years); top 10 in `impact_top_segments.csv`.

## Why, and is it supported

Two changes drive the movements. The current tariff charges BonusMalus 61-65 more than 66-80, a reversal of the no-claims scale; the proposed tariff merges 61-80 so premium never falls as BonusMalus rises (DECISIONS D039). This is the largest single source of change. The proposed tariff also adds three BonusMalus interactions: by driver age, for brand B12, and for a group of mainly urban and southern regions.

Observed loss cost on the holdout, which neither tariff was fitted on, is capped claims plus the flat large-loss load (all-claims ratios are in the table file). In every band except the largest increases, the proposed premium is closer to experience than the current one. Above +20% the proposed tariff overshoots (1.16 against current and 0.89 against proposed), and so does the merged band at BonusMalus 66-70. Band ratios carry sampling error of roughly +/-5% to +/-13% (95%).

## Capping trade-off

A +/-15% cap on year-one change, not re-balanced, changes revenue by -0.4%. Re-balanced to revenue neutrality (scale 1.0051 before capping), it delivers 77.9% of the intended movement and keeps 102.4% of the holdout Gini improvement; 18.3% of exposure sits at the cap. The largest moves add little ranking power on the holdout, consistent with the overshoot above +20%. Holdout Gini is noisy, so this supports a cap rather than proves one.

## Before implementation

- Retention and elasticity: the analysis is static; large increases may lapse and change the mix. No demand data.
- Competitor position: large decreases may already be below market; large increases may not be achievable.
- Regulatory and fairness review: region and density can proxy protected characteristics; the age interactions move young and older drivers. No fairness testing was done.
- BonusMalus drives most movements and is itself a record of claims (LIMITATIONS).
- A multi-year transition for policies at the cap.
